notes: Resource count measures distinct learning sources, not videos, datasets, models, courses, or lessons contained within a source.
A public URL, open-access article, dataset card, or metadata record does not establish permission to download, redistribute, retain, or train.
FreeCodeCamp software code license does not automatically license every curriculum asset or third-party media.
YouTube captions.list returns track metadata, not caption text. captions.download requires OAuth and permission to edit the video; never bypass this restriction.
Tolkien works remain copyright-controlled. Study scholarly metadata, abstracts, authorized resources and licensed materials; do not bulk-copy novels, appendices, maps, audio, or proprietary lexicons.
Tolkien Gateway, LotR Project and Encyclopedia of Arda are secondary reference aids, not authoritative canon.
Verify every URL, current availability, license, publisher, date, update cadence and terms during source admission.

specialized_study_tracks.title: Tolkien Studies: Philology, Mythopoeia, Worldbuilding and Literary Analysis
specialized_study_tracks.purpose: Teach scholarly methods for studying Tolkien's linguistic creativity, philological method, mythology, literary structure, archival history and reception using rights-cleared secondary scholarship and catalog metadata.
learning_outcomes: Explain the relationship between philology, historical linguistics and literary worldbuilding.
Analyze mythopoeia and invented-world design as literary concepts without reproducing protected expression.
Compare high-level narrative, thematic and linguistic techniques across independently selected public-domain works.
Use archival catalogs, bibliographies and peer-reviewed scholarship with citations and provenance.
Distinguish primary texts, scholarly commentary, bibliographic metadata and public-domain comparative materials.

lesson_sequence.lab: Compare phonology, morphology and language-family concepts using independently licensed linguistic datasets
Write an original comparative analysis using public-domain myths and peer-reviewed scholarship
Create an original worldbuilding schema that does not reuse Tolkien characters, settings, languages or distinctive protected elements
Design a bibliographic record with source edition, archive, rights status and citation trail
Model public catalog metadata into a graph with entities, citations and uncertainty labels
Compare two peer-reviewed interpretations and record evidence, scope and limitations
Produce an original, fully cited scholarly research brief and pass a source-provenance/safety review

specialized_study_tracks.completion_rule: A lesson is complete only after an original learner-authored artifact, source citations, provenance check and rubric result are recorded. Catalog discovery alone is not learning evidence.
specialized_study_tracks.truth_boundary: This is a study curriculum, not a licensed Tolkien corpus, transcript collection, model-training dataset, or claim that Buddy has completed the lessons.
